sentences.text: The petitioner is present before this Court and has been identified by his counsel Mr. Navin Prakash and Investigating Officer (IO) WSI Sumedha from Police Station Shalimar Bagh, North West, Delhi.

6. Brief facts of the present case are that marriage between petitioner and respondent no. 2 was solemnized on 20.06.2011 according to Hindu Rites and ceremonies and no child was born out of the said wedlock.

It is stated that due to temperamental differences, on the complaint of respondent no. 2, an FIR bearing No. 221/2013 was registered at Police Station Shalimar Bagh, North West,
Delhi for offences punishable under Sections 498A/406 of the IPC against petitioners.

sentences.text: During the pendency of the present FIR, both the parties had amicably settled their disputes before the Counselling Cell, Family Courts, North-West, Rohini, New Delhi vide Settlement Deed dated 27.07.2023 entered into between them.

entities.text: Counselling Cell, Family Courts, North-West, Rohini
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 7. On a query made by this Court, respondent no.2 who has been identified by the IO, has categorically stated that she has entered into compromise out of her own free will and without any pressure, coercion or threat.
It is also stated by respondent No.2 that the entire dispute has been amicably settled between the parties vide Settlement Deed dated 27.07.2023 entered into between them.

8. It is submitted that respondent no.2 has settled all her claims in respect of her dowry articles,
stridhan, marriage expenses, jewellery, gift items and claims of past, present and future maintenance and permanent alimony with petitioner No.1 and other family members.

9. The petitioner had paid a sum of Rs. 20,00,000/- in three installments in the following manner:

First installment of Rs.7 Lakhs paid to respondent no. 2 in the first motion petition.
b. Second installment of Rs. 7 Lakhs paid to respondent no. 2 at the time of second motion petition.
c. Third/Final instalment of Rs. 6 lakhs to be paid at the time of quashing of the FIR before the Hon ble High Court at New Delhi.

10. Today, the complainant who is present in Court states that she has received the last and final instalment of Rs. 6 Lacs today, i.e., 08.11.2023 vide DD No. 0071103 drawn on HDFC Bank and has no objection if the FIR is quashed.

11. In view of the above fact that the parties have amicably resolved their differences of their own free will, and without any coercion, no useful purpose will be served by continuing the proceedings,
